room_name: La garde-robe · The dressing room
note: painting repainted (gold-framed mirror replaced) to add a mauve-pink door with two gold stars (to repetition, La salle de répétition); alt updated; its 6 word cards recropped

room_name: La salle de répétition · The rehearsal room
hook: "fee-ZEEK": a sporty girl stretches as her soda FIZZES over and she squeals EEK: a PHYSICAL warm-up: fee-ZEEK ≈ FIZZ-EEK
note: Physical (l'exercice physique); also sporty. Le physique = looks, build (un physique agréable); la physique = physics.

room_name: La salle de répétition · The rehearsal room
hook: "voh-lohn-TEHR": a girl's hand shoots up to VOLUNTEER to sew the big TEAR in the curtain: VOLUN-TEAR: voh-lohn-TEHR ≈ VOLUN-TEAR
note: Voluntary, deliberate; of a person, strong-willed, determined. Un or une volontaire = a volunteer.

room_name: La salle de répétition · The rehearsal room
hook: "kor-DYAHL": a smiling lady chats so warmly on the old phone, twirling the CORD and spinning the DIAL: CORD-DIAL: kor-DYAHL ≈ CORD-DIAL
note: Cordial, warm, friendly (un accueil cordial); cordialement = kind regards (end of an email).

room_name: La salle de répétition · The rehearsal room
hook: "may-DYOKR": a so-so magician pulls a smelly SOCK, not a rabbit, out of his hat: MEDIOCRE: may-DYOKR ≈ MEDIOCRE
note: Mediocre, poor, second-rate; negative about work or people (un élève médiocre = a weak student).

room_name: La salle de répétition · The rehearsal room
hook: "day-ree-ZWAHR": a boy knight in foil armor holds up a floppy cheese-stick sword, a DAIRY SWORD, and everyone giggles: how paltry!: day-ree-ZWAHR ≈ DAIRY-SWAR(D)
note: Paltry, laughably small (un salaire dérisoire = a pitiful wage); also futile, pointless. Negative.

room_name: La salle de répétition · The rehearsal room
hook: "preh-SAHN": the stage manager PRESSES the red button ON the clock again and again: hurry! PRESS-ON: preh-SAHN ≈ PRESS-ON
note: Pressing, urgent (un besoin pressant); of a person, insistent or pushy (se faire pressant).

room_name: La salle de répétition · The rehearsal room
hook: "an-DEENY": a boy-king in a paper crown sulks IN a shabby little stage DINGHY: so unworthy of a king! IN-DINGHY: an-DEENY ≈ IN-DINGHY
note: Unworthy (indigne de = unworthy of); also disgraceful, shameful (une conduite indigne). Strongly negative.

room_name: Le cabinet des timbres · The stamp room
hook: "sway-DWAH": a boy SWAYS and sings DOO-WAH, waving a little blue-and-yellow flag of Sweden: SWAY-DWAH: sway-DWAH ≈ SWAY-DWAH
note: Swedish; le suédois = the Swedish language; un Suédois, une Suédoise = a Swede (capitalized). Suede leather is le daim.

room_name: Le cabinet des timbres · The stamp room
hook: "eer-lahn-DEH": a girl hugs a pot of shamrocks by the green, white and orange flag of IRELAND and cheers AY!: IRELAND-AY: eer-lahn-DEH ≈ IRELAND-AY
note: Irish; l'irlandais = the Irish language; un Irlandais, une Irlandaise = an Irish person (capitalized).

room_name: Le cabinet des timbres · The stamp room
hook: "mah-LEH": MA LAYS a bright batik cloth on the table beside the flag of Malaysia: MA-LAYS: mah-LEH ≈ MA-LAY(S)
note: Malay (le malais = the Malay language); Malaysian is malaisien. Not malaise (un malaise = discomfort, a dizzy spell).

room_name: Le cabinet des timbres · The stamp room
hook: "goh-LWAH": a girl unrolls an old map of ancient GAUL dotted with round thatched huts and gasps WAH!: GAUL-WAH: goh-LWAH ≈ GAUL-WAH
note: Gaulish, of the ancient Gauls; often 'very French' (le coq gaulois). Also bawdy, ribald (l'humour gaulois).

room_name: Le cabinet des timbres · The stamp room
hook: "mehk-see-KAN": a boy holds up a tin CAN with a little cactus growing in it, beside the green, white and red flag of Mexico: MEXI-CAN: mehk-see-KAN ≈ MEXI-CAN
note: Mexican; un Mexicain, une Mexicaine = a Mexican person (capitalized).

room_name: Le cabinet des timbres · The stamp room
hook: "nor-MAHN": NORMAN the dairy farmer shows off a round Camembert box and a toy black-and-white cow from Normandy: NOR-MAN: nor-MAHN ≈ NOR-MAN (Norman)
note: Norman, from Normandy (la Normandie). Une réponse de Normand = a noncommittal 'maybe yes, maybe no' answer.

room_name: Le cabinet des timbres · The stamp room
hook: "BREWSK": a gruff clerk thumps his rubber stamp down so BRUSQUELY that the postcards jump: BRUSK: BREWSK ≈ BRUSK
note: Abrupt, curt (un ton brusque = a curt tone); also sudden (un changement brusque). Negative about a manner.

room_name: Le cabinet des timbres · The stamp room
hook: "mewl-tee-koh-LOR": a girl holds up a patchwork quilt in every color: MULTI-COLOR: mewl-tee-koh-LOR ≈ MULTI-COLOR
note: Multicolored, many-colored. Same form for masculine and feminine.

room_name: La salle des noces · The wedding hall
hook: "NOBL": a stately grandfather with a crest sash and a monocle stands tall and NOBLE: NOBL ≈ NOBLE
note: Noble, of the nobility; also high-minded. Of materials: fine, natural (le bois, un matériau noble).

room_name: La salle des noces · The wedding hall
hook: "mah-tree-moh-NYAHL": the bride and groom hold hands under the flower arch: MATRIMONIAL: mah-tree-moh-NYAHL ≈ MATRIMONIAL
note: Matrimonial, of marriage: une agence matrimoniale = a marriage bureau; le régime matrimonial = the couple's property arrangement.

room_name: La salle des noces · The wedding hall
hook: "ee-ray-zees-TEEBL": a girl just cannot resist the chocolate fountain and sneaks a finger toward it: IRRESISTIBLE: ee-ray-zees-TEEBL ≈ IRRESISTIBLE
note: Irresistible; of a person, charming. Une envie irrésistible = an overwhelming urge.

room_name: La salle des noces · The wedding hall
hook: "oh-noh-RAHBL": an HONEST boy hands a lost wallet back to its owner: ON-OR-ABLE, honorable: oh-noh-RAHBL ≈ HONOR-ABLE
note: Honorable, decent; also respectable, adequate (un résultat honorable = a creditable result).

room_name: La salle des noces · The wedding hall
hook: "UNBL": the gardener who grew all the roses bows shyly, cap in hand, as guests clap: HUMBLE: UNBL ≈ HUMBLE (silent h)
note: Humble, modest; also lowly (d'humble origine = of humble birth). À mon humble avis = in my humble opinion.

room_name: La salle des noces · The wedding hall
hook: "lwah-YAHL": a grandma and grandpa, married fifty years and still side by side, clap for the couple: LWAH-YAL, loyal: lwah-YAHL ≈ LOYAL
note: Loyal, faithful; also fair, honest (un adversaire loyal = a fair opponent).

room_name: Le club de jeux · The games club
hook: "ah-bee-luh-TAY": a girl stacks a tall, wobbly domino tower with real ABILITY: ABILI-TAY: ah-bee-luh-TAY ≈ ABILI-TAY (ability)
note: Skill, dexterity; also cleverness, a clever move (une habileté = a ploy).

room_name: Le club de jeux · The games club
hook: "bah-VAHR": the club parrot chatters nonstop, blah blah: BLAH-VAR: bah-VAHR ≈ BLAH-VAR
note: Chatty, talkative; also indiscreet, a blabbermouth. Un bavard, une bavarde = a chatterbox.

room_name: Le club de jeux · The games club
hook: "geh-RYAY": GARRY leads his toy army of tin soldiers and cannons across the rug, cheering YAY!: GARRY-YAY: geh-RYAY ≈ GARRY-YAY
note: Warlike, martial, belligerent. Un guerrier = a warrior.

room_name: Le club de jeux · The games club
hook: "os-TEEL": a pet hedgehog bristles all its spines at a wind-up robot: HOSTILE: os-TEEL ≈ HOSTILE
note: Hostile, unfriendly, opposed (hostile à un projet = opposed to a plan).

room_name: Le club de jeux · The games club
hook: "moh-DEHST": the girl who just won the board game smiles shyly and shrugs while her friends clap: MODEST: moh-DEHST ≈ MODEST
note: Modest, unassuming; of an amount, small, humble (un salaire modeste).

room_name: Le club de jeux · The games club
hook: "skahn-dah-LEUH": a boy is caught with an extra card sliding out of his sleeve and the table gasps: SCANDAL-UH: skahn-dah-LEUH ≈ SCANDAL-UH
note: Scandalous, shocking; outrageous (un prix scandaleux = an outrageous price).

room_name: Le club de jeux · The games club
hook: "prew-DAHN": a careful boy plays ping-pong in a helmet and knee pads, just in case: PRUDENT: prew-DAHN ≈ PRUDENT
note: Careful, cautious, sensible. Not prudish (prude).

room_name: Le hall d'entrée · The entrance hall
change: American spelling (gray, cozy, favor, meager, multicolored)
hook: "OM": a bearded MAN sits cross-legged on a cushion under the stairs chanting "OM": OM = OM
note: Also mankind (l'homme = humanity) and, with an adjective, a man of a kind (un homme d'affaires = a businessman).

room_name: La salle des âges · The hall of ages
change: American spelling (gray, cozy, favor, meager, multicolored)
hook: "an-dee-vee-DEW": in a row of identical gray toy penguins on the shelf, one INDIVIDUAL wears a red scarf and waves: an-dee-vee-DEW = INDIVIDU(al)
note: Often mildly negative in news and police talk: un individu = a suspicious person, 'an individual'.

room_name: L'atelier des portraits · The portrait studio
change: American spelling (gray, cozy, favor, meager, multicolored)
hook: "mee-NYOHN": a cute kitten curls up in a basket of ONIONS and the painter coos "my ONION!": mee-NYOHN ≈ my ONION
note: Also sweet, kind (c'est mignon de ta part = that's sweet of you).

room_name: La salle du courage · The courage gym
change: American spelling (gray, cozy, favor, meager, multicolored)
hook: "tee-MEED": a TIMID rabbit hides behind a big TEA pot on the bench: tee-MEED ≈ TEA + (ti)MID
note: Shy, bashful.

room_name: Le salon de thé · The tea room
change: American spelling (gray, cozy, favor, meager, multicolored)
hook: "fah-voh-RAHBL": a man taps the barometer and the needle swings to the sun: FAVOR-ABLE weather: fah-voh-RAHBL ≈ FAVOR-ABLE
note: Favorable; être favorable à = to be in favor of.

room_name: La garde-robe · The dressing room
change: American spelling (gray, cozy, favor, meager, multicolored)
hook: "pahr-SYEHL": a jacket with only ONE sleeve sewn on: only PARTIAL: par-SYEL ≈ PARTIAL
note: Partial, in part (une vue partielle). False friend: French partial means biased. Un partiel = a university exam.

room_name: La garde-robe · The dressing room
change: American spelling (gray, cozy, favor, meager, multicolored)
hook: "MOSH": a boy in a lumpy, clashing snowman sweater so ugly the others want to MOSH it away: MOSH: MOSH ≈ MOSH
note: Ugly (informal); also rotten, a shame (c'est moche = that's too bad). Rude about a person.

room_name: La garde-robe · The dressing room
change: American spelling (gray, cozy, favor, meager, multicolored)
hook: "MEHGR": a skinny grayhound in a little coat bares its teeth: MAY GRR!: MEH-gruh ≈ MAY GRR
note: Thin, skinny (can be unkind about a person); also low-fat (fromage maigre) and meager (un maigre salaire).
